call_input.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Create exactly one finished, full-bleed, flat portrait poster, aspect ratio 2:3. This is the artwork itself, no room mockup, frame, panels, contact sheet or alternate versions.
요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Concept: at night a modest living flowering plant becomes a garden-sized presence through its enlarged cast shadow. Make the causal plant-and-shadow pairing unmistakable, rather than an unrelated floral silhouette.

Scene and composition: a nearly frontal photographic view of a matte, cool blue-gray plaster garden wall and a narrow strip of dark ground at its bottom. A living white night-blooming plant grows from a small dark soil crevice near the lower-left edge; three slender branching stems, a few clearly formed oval leaves, and three open white five-petaled flowers. Show the plant clearly at roughly the lower third of the poster, with real stems meeting their rooted base. The very same three flower heads, stems and leaves cast one much larger shadow across the wall, moving upward and to the right and occupying most of the upper-right field. Keep each flower-head silhouette recognizably paired with its smaller visible source. The shadow starts continuously at the plant's base and expands with distance, not three disconnected decorative black flowers. Frame the enlarged uppermost shadow near, but not clipped by, the top edge.

Lighting and materials: one plausible low, compact warm-white light source just out of frame to the lower-left, closer to the plant than the wall, produces the upward-right enlarged cast shadow. Its highlights appear on the plant's left-facing petal edges and leaf surfaces. Matte, soft white petals, restrained deep olive stems and leaves, dark soil. The wall is a desaturated slate blue in nighttime ambient light, gently brighter at the lower-left, progressively quieter toward the upper-right. No circular spotlight graphic, luminous aura or visible lamp. Shadows have relatively defined structure near the base and subtly softer contours farther away. Use restrained photographic grain and credible shallow plaster texture, not scratches or distressed paper printed across every element.

Typography and spatial relationship: the title is a single horizontal line across the middle-lower wall, above the smaller flower heads and below the largest projected blossom heads. Its left boundary aligns near the outer extent of the living plant, while the line extends into the width occupied by the larger shadow, acting as a measured bridge between the small plant and its garden-sized presence. Bold, clean Korean sans-serif typography in soft white, generously legible but proportional to this image. Keep the complete title in one line, with visibly correct word spaces, intact Hangul strokes and enough contrast; do not let stems or dark shadow destroy letter shapes. The plant-to-shadow diagonal remains visible around the type.
The only printed text, exactly once, verbatim: 밤에 피는 정원

Reading path: first the large cast flower forms and the complete readable title, then the smaller illuminated blossoms and their continuous stems, so the viewer recognizes that one small flowering growth produces the larger garden presence. A quiet, precise nighttime atmosphere supported by this scale change.
Do not add any other text, captions, dates, labels, symbols, quotation marks, numbers, logos, watermark, decorative marks, stars, moon, extra flowers, or ornamental borders. No duplicated title and no pseudo-lettering in shadows. Preserve the single flat poster and 2:3 ratio.

residuals: Individual petal-count and leaf-silhouette correspondence is uncertain; possible simplified shadow petals.
Pale lines within shadow flower centers have uncertain physical explanation.
Readable conventional typography connects the two scales mostly through placement.
